title: Wire Cursor dedup, incremental rescan, and doctor
description:
Wire the shared frameworks into the Cursor adapter: dedup by composerId and native bubbleId keys (a composer appearing in both old and new indexes is one conversation); incremental rescan via per-DB watermarks with a createdAt watermark plus overlap margin; stream queries by key prefix (never SELECT star; ignore checkpoint and messageRequestContext blobs — global DBs reach tens of GB); doctor checks reporting missing keys after Cursor updates.

Done when: duplicated index entries count once; rescan equals cold scan; a large fixture streams without loading blobs; doctor runs on a real Mac.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Wired shared frameworks: dedup by composerId and native bubbleId keys (a composer in both indexes counts once — tested), per-DB incremental rescans via a createdAt watermark floor with a 60s overlap margin (sqliteRescanFloor in scan-state.ts, floor plumbed through extractComposerBubbles), prefix-streamed queries that never load blobs, and doctorCursor reporting global/workspace DB presence plus agent-transcript sessions. Rescan-equals-cold-scan asserted at scan level. Real-Mac doctor run remains open under KDATAP-e9aa3c. Outcome: green.
